leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members prefer a single-part prize for the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye. They share the two names and the case that magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift by design, that roughly 1e-18 uncertainty has been reproduced and compared across several laboratories, and that the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes covered neighbouring steps. The citations differ in emphasis: some stress a new regime of precision, others a new measurement capability or physics beyond metrology. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Olsson and I say we rely on recollection of the priority history, and Johansson and Pearce moved to B007 after rereading the opening ballots (Johansson from B058, Pearce from B039). Several supporters hold it as a first choice with reservations rather than without them.

Two members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, with near-identical three-name configurations. They share the view that the 2011 continuum-model prediction and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity form an unusually direct theory-experiment loop, reproduced across moire platforms. They differ in citation wording and in emphasis, Eriksson on the surprise in a material and electronic-structure engagement, Mehlig on the analytically transparent mechanism. Both name the unresolved pairing mechanism and the credit gap (Cao and the first experimental authors; earlier twisted-bilayer theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto) as their strongest reservations. Both name B007 as a fallback, and B001 is the most frequently named alternative to B007 among the other six.

areas_of_agreement: All eight preferred configurations are single-part prizes, and no member proposes a two-part prize in round 1.
B007 and B001 are the only two ballot IDs in any member's preferred configuration. Six members prefer B007 and two prefer B001, and each of those two names B007 as an alternative.
Every member who prefers B007 uses the same two laureates, Katori and Ye, and every member who prefers B001 uses the same three, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer.
Members on both sides state the same B007 reservations: instrument or metrology versus discovery, possible overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and the SI second not yet being redefined.
Members on both sides state the same B001 reservations: the pairing mechanism is unsettled, and the three-name limit omits earlier theory and first experimental authors.
Several members rely on recollection and not on checked documents for priority questions on B007 and B001, and ask for the historical record to be examined.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock counts as a discovery or an invention that opens a new measurement regime. Supporters answer that it has already produced physics (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on varying constants, dark-matter searches), while Eriksson, who ranked it fifth, weighs possible overlap with earlier metrology prizes.

Whether the circuit QED candidate B058 (Johansson's opening first choice, no longer in his preferred configuration) is distinct from the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits. Danielsson reads the 2025 prize as already covering that platform, and Johansson himself raises the same concern.

Whether the unresolved origin of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is a scientific dispute that bears on the prize, or only a feature of a young field. Eriksson and Mehlig treat the observed phase diagram and its reproduction as sufficient, and Danielsson and Olsson weigh the open mechanism against the clocks.

Whether IceCube source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane) are solid enough to add to the diffuse-flux discovery, with independent confirmation from KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD still limited. Only I ranked B039 first at opening, and I no longer prefer it in round 1.
attribution_disputes: B007: whether Katori and Ye alone fairly represent the field. Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom, the JILA collaborators and the ion-clock groups are raised as possible omissions by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and me, and no member says they would add a name.

B001: whether Bistritzer should be included. Danielsson's own two-name idea would drop him while conceding the 2011 prediction was a joint calculation, and Eriksson, Mehlig and the other B001 configurations keep all three names.

B001: how to treat Cao and the first experimental authors, groups such as Dean, Watanabe and Taniguchi, and earlier twisted-bilayer theory. Eriksson and Mehlig flag both points, and Olsson flags the earlier flat-band theory. None resolves them.
B039: how to split credit among Halzen, Karle and Spiering in a collaboration of this size. Several members noted that any two or three names simplify the collaboration's credit.
B058: Wallraff made the first strong-coupling circuit QED experiment and is outside the three credited names. Johansson, Danielsson and Olsson all note this.
maturity_disputes: B007: the redefinition of the second has not happened, so some impact is prospective. Several supporters read the planned redefinition as evidence of community acceptance, and Kroll also asks whether a prize before the redefinition is timely or slightly early.

B001: the field is about eight years old. Olsson called the timing early but defensible and Danielsson called it quite mature for its age but slightly early. Mehlig names the optical lattice clock as the more mature choice if the committee finds the discovery not yet settled.
B039 and B058: IceCube source associations are recent, and B058 is close in time to the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and works with Chalmers superconducting-circuit groups, and Chalmers hosted 2025 laureates Martinis and Clarke. He states he should recuse on B058 and that his earlier support for it should be discounted.

Olsson works in electron microscopy and says she would recuse on B030, which she ranked first at opening and left out of her preferred configuration. She also holds a University of Tokyo fellowship since 2025, where Katori works, with no personal or research connection to Katori or Ye apparent from her profile.

Kroll spent a year of his PhD in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and Hall was Jun Ye's mentor at JILA. He sees no formal conflict on B007, flags it to the chair and will recuse if the committee judges that necessary. He also works in atomic physics and quantum memories, adjacent to B008, B015 and B005.
Lindroth is a close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier and notes atomic-physics proximity to B007 and B015, with no specific conflict requiring recusal.
Eriksson notes that his electron-structure theory work is close to, but does not overlap with, the moire-materials community, and he names no conflict.

My own disclosure: I belong to the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations, and B039 (IceCube) is in my broad field of astroparticle physics, but I see no collaboration with IceCube or its credited individuals. I rank B007 and B001 as having no specific conflict for me.
Danielsson, as Secretary, has a procedural role in commissioning expert reports and notes that this is not a personal connection to any candidate. Mehlig reports no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B007, can the committee state in the citation why the optical lattice clock is a distinct achievement from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and a discovery of new measurement physics and not an instrument advance?

For B007, do the first lattice-clock publications support Katori and Ye as the two names, or do Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom or ion-clock groups need to be added or mentioned? What would an expert report on the historical record need to establish?
Should a prize be awarded before or after the redefinition of the SI second, and is that an argument about maturity or only about timing?
For B001, which of Eriksson and Mehlig's three names would each remove if only two were possible, and does the citation need to name the 2011 prediction and the 2018 experiments separately?

For B001, how should the committee weigh the unresolved pairing mechanism, device-to-device variation and the omission of Cao and earlier twisted-bilayer theory against the strong cross-laboratory reproduction?
Is B001 considered by the members who prefer B007 a candidate for the same year, a later year or a different prize, and would any member move to B001 if the experts confirm the credit history?
Given that no member currently prefers B039, B058, B023, B030 or B008, would any member reinstate one of them in round 2 and on what credit or maturity grounds, or should they be set aside?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 configurations, six members prefer B007 (Katori and Ye) and two prefer B001 (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer), and every member names the other as an alternative or fallback in some form: all eight proposals are single-part, and the open points are mainly credit and timing, not a disagreement about the science itself. B007's reservations are mostly category and overlap with earlier prizes, plus completeness of credit. B001's reservations are the unsettled mechanism and credit for earlier theory and first experiments. Several of the stated positions rest on recollection of priority and not on checked documents, so round 2 should say which of these points can be settled from the record and which are matters of judgement.
